A Unimodal Shape

Source: R/shape.R
shape_unimodal.Rd

Constructs the shape that makes a smooth increase up to a mode and decrease after it, for scs().

Usage

shape_unimodal(link = linkfunctions7::log_link(), mode = NULL, index = NULL)

Arguments

link

A linkfunctions7 link onto \((0, \infty)\).

mode

NULL, or a single number: the value of the covariate at which the mode is placed.

index

NULL, or the index \(M\) itself, which a fitting layer sets on the versions it tries. It takes precedence over mode.

Value

An S7 object of class ShapeUnimodal, inheriting from shape_constraint.

Details

The mode sits at a Greville abscissa \(\xi_M\) of the basis: the slopes of the coefficients are \(+g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\) up to index \(M\) and \(-g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\) after it, so the coefficients, and with them the curve, rise to a single maximum. \(M = 1\) is a decreasing curve and \(M = K\) an increasing one. The penalty of scs() is one random walk on \(\gamma\) through the mode, whose null space is the same for every \(M\), so fits at different \(M\) are compared by their criterion.

With mode given, \(M\) is the index of the Greville abscissa nearest to it and the model is fitted once. With mode = NULL the fitting layer chooses \(M\): a pilot fit with s() in place of the term gives the abscissa nearest to its maximum, \(M_0\), and the model is fitted at the indices \(M_0 - 2, \dots, M_0 + 2\); the best criterion decides (see term_pilot() and term_variants()).

See also

scs(), shape_increasing().

Examples

shape_unimodal()
#> <shape: unimodal, link = log>
shape_unimodal(mode = 0.4)
#> <shape: unimodal, link = log, mode = 0.4>
